name: Nubia Air Pro 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7100 with a 144Hz AMOLED, bypass charging and a 5000mAh battery is a strong mid-range gaming combination — smooth play in most titles at high settings, with only the most demanding games needing a step down.

name: Nubia Neo 3 5G
gaming_notes: The Unisoc T8300 is a modest gaming chip, but shoulder triggers, a 120Hz display, bypass charging and a 6000mAh battery make sustained casual and mid-range gaming comfortable — heavy titles will need medium settings.

name: Dcode Cygnal Evo 2
gaming_notes: An entry-level octa-core chip with 4GB of RAM and a 90Hz HD+ screen — only light casual games will run smoothly; demanding titles will lag.

name: Nubia Neo 5 Pro 5G
gaming_notes: The UNISOC T9100 with Mali-G57 graphics is a modest gaming chip, so heavy titles need medium settings, but the 120Hz OLED, shoulder triggers, bypass charging and 80W top-ups make it a capable casual-to-mid gaming phone with a much better screen than most rivals at this price.

name: Nubia Neo 5 Max PadPhone 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7100 is a mid-range chip, but the 990Hz shoulder triggers, 30,000mm² cooling, bypass charging and 7,100mAh battery make sustained gaming genuinely strong — the 120Hz 7.5-inch screen shows more of the game than any rival at this price. Heavy titles will still need medium settings.

name: Vivo Y32
gaming_notes: The entry-level Unisoc T7300 and HD+ display keep casual games smooth, and Game Boost mode helps, but this is a battery-first phone, not a gaming one.

name: Honor Play 10
gaming_notes: The Helio G81 with 3-4GB RAM handles casual games and everyday titles at low settings only — this is a basics phone, not a gaming device.

name: Oppo Find X10
gaming_notes: The 3nm Dimensity 9600M with a 144Hz AMOLED and 7,150mAh battery (80W charging) is flagship-class for gaming, though the Find X10 is tuned for cameras first — no dedicated gaming triggers or active cooling.

name: Samsung Galaxy A08 LTE
gaming_notes: The Helio G99 runs popular titles like PUBG Mobile and Free Fire smoothly at balanced settings on the 90Hz display.

name: Tecno Pova Curve 2 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 7100 with Ice Cooling 3.0, a 144Hz curved AMOLED (2160Hz instant touch sampling) and bypass charging make this a strong mid-range gaming pick — TECNO claims 90 minutes of stable Free Fire at 60fps. The 8,000mAh battery stretches long sessions, though 45W charging needs ~82 minutes for a full refill.

name: Motorola Moto g37 5G
gaming_notes: The Dimensity 6300 runs PUBG Mobile smoothly on medium settings; the 120Hz LCD keeps casual games fluid. Don't expect high-refresh competitive gaming at this price.

name: Sony Xperia 10 VIII
gaming_notes: The Snapdragon 6 Gen 3 handles everyday games at medium settings on the 120Hz OLED, but demanding 3D titles stutter and push the Adreno 710 to its limits.
